title: Low-Cost Cryo-Light Microscopy Stage Fabrication for Correlated Light/Electron Microscopy
protocol: Place the aluminum heat sink inside the 22.96 cm pie pan approximately 2 cm from the side of the pan.
Mark holes for the aluminum heat sink using a black marker pen.
Drill pilot holes for each marked position using a #17 drill bit for the aluminum heat sink holes.
Mount the aluminum heat sink using 5 - #10, 1.9 cm flat head slotted bolts and corresponding nuts as well as 15 - #10 washers.
Place two washers beneath the aluminum block and one on the backside of the pie pan for each hole.
Insert 3 - #4, 0.95 cm round slotted bolts and corresponding nuts from the backside of the pie pan to act as the cryo-grid box mount.
Check to make sure all mounting bolts are firmly tightened.
Tape 4 chopsticks together in pairs with one chopstick atop another.
Tape each pair to opposite edges of the cake pan to act as spacers.
Wet the top and bottom surface of the cake and pie pans respectively with ddH2O.
Fill the cake pan with two layers of insulating spray foam.
Wet each layer before going to the next step.
Press the pie pan into the foam.
Flip the pans upside down and press on the cake pan until the spacers contact the pie pan.
Place any weighted object atop the cake pan and let sit overnight to cure.
With a serrated knife, cut away the excess dried insulating spray foam from the edge of the pans.
Remove the chopsticks.
Remove the cake pan from the pie pan.
The pie pan with aluminum heat sink is now insulated and will be referred to as the "cryogenic stage".
Place a transparent plastic clipboard over the top of the cryogenic stage.
Mark with a black marker the location of the cryo-grid box mount by drawing a circle approximately 1.5 times the diameter of a single round cryo-grid box.
Cut out hole with a 1.9 cm (3/4") hole saw.
This clipboard will be referred to as the "loading screen".
Put a new transparent clipboard atop of the cryogenic stage and place on the microscope with the heat sink directly under the objective lenses.
With a black marker, mark the path of the objectives as they rotate.
Cut along the marked line removing a half circle from the edge of the clipboard using a jigsaw or hole saw.
Cut a 1.9 cm (3/4") hole away from the half circle for refilling liquid nitrogen.
Dilute log phase yeast cells grown in synthetic complete media to an appropriate concentration of 1x10^6 cells/mL in water.
Pipette 2 mL of diluted yeast onto a R2/1 400 mesh holey carbon coated copper cryo-EM grid and allow to adsorb for 15 seconds.
Blot away excess liquid from the grid surface by touching the back of the grid to a torn piece of soft cellulose tissue (Kimwipe) for 2 seconds.
Wash the grid with 3 μL drops of water if necessary, and blot away as in step 3 using torn tissue paper (Kimwipe).
Load the sample into the pneumatic plunge freezer and wash the hanging grid as in step 2.4.
Plunge the grid into liquid ethane cooled by liquid nitrogen after blotting to remove excess water.
Fill the cryogenic stage with lN2 and quickly cover with the loading screen.
Transfer the metal in the cryogenic stage to lN2 temperature.
Transfer the cryo-grid box through the hole of the loading screen into the transfer mount.
Unscrew the cryo-grid box from its holder and remove the holder.
Refill lN2 in the cryogenic stage to just below the top of the aluminum heat sink.
Pre-cool the tweezer tip in lN2.
Transfer your grid(s) onto the flat viewing surface of the aluminum heat sink with tweezers, using the hole of the loading screen.
Place the transparent viewing screen atop the loading screen.
Slowly remove the loading screen by sliding it underneath the viewing screen.
Minimize air currents around the microscope.
Rotate the objective lenses into the cold nitrogen gas environment of the cryo-stage.
Scan for the sample on the flat heat sink viewing area using standard bright field light microscopy techniques.
Focus on the grid with a low magnification objective to find the center and take an overview image.
Focus in high magnification on an area of interest.
Acquire data with bright field, dark field, polarized light or fluorescence imaging.
Record the location of the area of interest on the low magnification bright field image for future correlation.
Load the sample grid into a cryo-EM transfer holder while keeping the specimen at liquid nitrogen temperature.
Insert the cryo-holder with sample grid into a Transmission Electron Microscope.
Find the center of the sample grid in a suitable low magnification view (50-500x nominal magnification).
Determine the relative orientation of the grid’s central copper tabs using previously collected low magnification cryo-LM data.
Identify exact areas of interest for correlation based on the determined orientation.
Proceed with microscope alignment.
Perform low-dose cryo-EM imaging and data collection.
